purpose: Define the physically consistent one-dimensional exit target implied by the same frozen NASA Wind-US conservative moments used to construct the reduced-domain inlet and signed source closures. This target is a computational-reference-derived moment match, not an experimental measurement and not a fit to the experimental exit profiles.

derivation.branch_policy: Solve the resulting quadratic for u and select the unique positive supersonic branch for the effective gas. The alternate positive subsonic root is retained only as a mathematical diagnostic and is not selected.

claim_boundary: This exit target is derived from the NASA Wind-US computational reference solution, not from the Burrows-Kurkov experimental probe profiles.

Mass-flux-weighted Mach, area-weighted pressure, and mass-flux-weighted temperature from a nonuniform two-dimensional section are not thermodynamically equivalent to a single one-dimensional primitive state and therefore are diagnostic-only comparisons.
The conservative moment-matched exit state is the correct internal consistency target for the reduced-order solver driven by the same reference-derived integral closures.
Agreement with this target verifies the reduction/solver consistency; it does not independently validate finite-rate chemistry or species transport.
